Only the six balanced patterns can distinguish order. For any balanced u and i,j>=2, a length-three common subsequence extends by the unused required letter to some balanced ordinary four-subsequence t in w; conversely ordinary t sharing three positions witnesses a one-jumble occurrence. The six singleton nonadjacency sets intersect into exactly the seven listed candidate missing patterns. Exact twofold symbol constraints exclude one candidate when a count exceeds 2 and the all-present candidate at (2,2); displayed witnesses realize every remaining type. This gives capped-cell counts 16*1 + 5*6 + 4*5 = 66 (the five 6-cells are (2,2),(2,3),(2,4),(3,2),(4,2)) and all-length represented-class counts 1,2,3,4,10,16,21,26,31 thereafter.
